meta.title: Periplo: x402 facilitator for Stellar
meta.description: Periplo verifies and settles x402 payments on Stellar that buyers sign themselves, sponsoring only the network fee. Open source, Apache-2.0, testnet only.
meta.ogAlt: Periplo. Sign a ceiling. Pay only for what you use.

hero.title: x402 payments on Stellar that charge only for what's used.
hero.lede: Periplo is an open-source, non-custodial x402 facilitator: in x402, the facilitator is the service that verifies and sends the payment the buyer signs. With upto, the buyer signs a spending ceiling once and only the real usage settles; the contract enforces the ceiling and its balance is zero after every settlement.
hero.uptoNote: We're proposing upto for Stellar inside the x402 standard, so any facilitator can use it the same way (open PR,
hero.testnetNote: Testnet only. Periplo does not operate on mainnet yet.

how.title: How it works
how.lede: A service answers HTTP 402 with its price. The buyer signs a payment; Periplo checks it and submits it to Stellar. Two schemes cover two ways of charging.

exact.title: exact: a fixed price
steps: The service asks for a fixed amount.
The buyer signs exactly that amount.
Periplo verifies it and settles that same amount.
exact.note: For requests with a known price, like one API call at a flat rate.

upto.title: upto: pay for real usage
steps: The buyer signs a spending ceiling once.
The service measures what was actually used.
Only the real amount is settled; the contract refunds the rest in the same transaction.
upto.note: For usage you only know afterwards: tokens generated, seconds of access, rows returned.

how.diagramLabel: Diagram comparing exact and upto settlement

facts.custodyText: The buyer signs each payment with their own key. The facilitator only pays network fees, refuses to start with a key that can move user funds, and is never the source or signer of a buyer's payment.
facts.discoveryText: Resources settled through Periplo can be cataloged so agents can find them by searching, not by knowing the URL in advance.
facts.uptoText: upto settles against the UptoSettlement contract on testnet. The public facilitator only advertises the schemes listed in its live status below.

sim.title: Try it yourself
sim.lede: Walk through the same flow with amounts generated locally. The simulation sends no transactions; you can also settle the same usage for real on testnet, where a project-owned demo buyer signs the ceiling. The real settlements are in the section above.
sim.hint: The buyer signs this maximum once. In the real flow it is an authorization signature over the contract. The simulation signs nothing; a real settlement is signed by the project's demo buyer, not by you.
sim.invalid: Enter an amount between {min} and {max} USDC with up to 7 decimals. The demo caps each real settlement at {max}.
sim.ceilingSummary: Authorized ceiling: {ceiling}. Simulated rate: {price} per generated token.
sim.reached: Ceiling reached: the service stops answering calls. The contract never allows charging more than what was signed.
sim.settledNote: Simulated: no transaction was sent. On testnet, this same result is a single call to settle that transfers the charged amount to the seller and refunds the rest to the buyer in the same transaction.

reference.title: A real equivalent settlement on testnet
reference.lede: The same pattern, run for real on the demo contract: a signed ceiling, a partial charge and the refund in a single transaction. Every value can be checked on-chain.
reference.fromEvents: Amounts read live from this transaction's settled event.
reference.fromEvidence: Static evidence record: the live event read is unavailable, or this transaction is older than the ~7 days of events the RPC keeps.

real.title: Settle for real on testnet
real.disclosure: This is a real settlement on Stellar testnet. The buyer is a test account owned by the project that signs the ceiling on your behalf; you sign nothing in your browser. Testnet USDC has no value.
real.tokensHint: You choose the usage in this demo. The server prices it at {price} per token and never trusts an amount from your browser. Enter 0 to use nothing: the whole ceiling goes back to the buyer. If the usage costs more than the ceiling, the charge stops at the ceiling.
real.pending: Signing the ceiling with the demo buyer and waiting for the transaction to be confirmed on testnet. This can take up to a minute…
real.capped: The usage would have cost {cost} {asset}, above the signed ceiling. The charge stopped at the ceiling: the contract does not allow charging more than what was signed.
real.zero: Nothing was used, so the charge is 0 and the whole ceiling went back to the buyer in the same transaction.
real.amountFromEvent: The charged amount is read from this transaction's settled event, not calculated in your browser.
real.fellBack: The real settlement did not complete, so this is the in-browser simulation (no transaction was sent). The evidence below is a real, earlier settlement.

security.title: Security
security.lede: How to report a vulnerability in Periplo, and what the design already protects against.
security.reportText: Report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting. Only the maintainers see the report until an advisory is published. Please do not open public issues with exploit details.
design: The facilitator refuses to start if its key could move users' assets.
It is never the source, operation source or signer of a buyer's payment; it only pays the network fee.
With upto, the buyer's signature covers a ceiling, and the contract rejects any settlement above it.
Every rejected payment returns an explicit reason.
